To construct a regular hexagon of side 40mm with one side horizontal:
1. Draw a horizontal base line $AB = 40\text{ mm}$.
2. At points $A$ and $B$, construct internal angles of $120^\circ$ using a protractor or compass.
3. Draw lines $AF$ and $BC$ of length $40\text{ mm}$ along these angles.
4. From points $F$ and $C$, draw arcs of radius $40\text{ mm}$ intersecting each other at point $D$, and similarly use $A$ and $B$ to find top vertex $E$ (or draw lines of $120^\circ$ from $F$ and $C$ meeting at top).
5. Join the vertices to complete the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ with base $AB$ horizontal.
proTip: The interior angle of a regular hexagon is $(6-2)\times 180^\circ / 6 = 120^\circ$.
